beats.narration_text: Hola. This is Liam, in for Bear. Most people type to the AI. But sometimes talking beats typing. The real question is not only how you talk to it, but when.

show.event: types 'How do I turn on voice mode'
backspaces the how-to into 'when should I talk to the AI instead of typing' on the spoken correction

props.text:
How do I turn on voice mode
in the AI app?
props.triggerWords: How do I turn on voice mode
props.replacementWords: when should I talk to the AI instead of typing

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive how-to question and corrects it to the real one: when to talk instead of type.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Voice mode: talking to the AI out loud instead of typing. A transcript: the written record of everything said in a voice conversation. A summary: the short text version of that conversation.

terms.meaning: talking to the AI out loud instead of typing
the written record of everything said in a voice conversation
the short text version of a conversation

beats.narration_text: Voice mode starts with one tap. Most AI apps, including Claude's, have it. Look for a microphone or waveform icon in the app you use. Tap it, and you are talking.

shot.visual_intent: A phone-style card holds a big mic button; three sound-wave arcs grow out of it; the label 'mic' sits beside it.
shot.motion_claim: A phone-style card holds a big mic button; three sound-wave arcs grow out of it; the label 'mic' sits beside it.

beats.narration_text: Tap the icon and speak in full sentences, the way you would to a person. The app writes down your words, the AI answers out loud, and you go back and forth like a phone call.

beats.narration_text: Talking wins when you are thinking out loud. Brainstorming a project, naming a business, planning a trip. Say half-formed ideas and let the AI catch them, sort them, and play them back to you.

shot.visual_intent: A head with thought dots rising; waves carry them to an idea bulb that lights with a terracotta glow.

beats.narration_text: It wins when your hands are busy. Cooking is the classic: flour on your fingers, a recipe question in your head. Ask out loud, get the answer out loud, and never touch the screen.

beats.narration_text: It wins when you need to rehearse. A job interview, a hard conversation, a phone call you are dreading. Say it out loud to the AI first, and hear how it lands.

shot.visual_intent: Two heads face each other with waves between them; a terracotta check lands above the listener.

beats.narration_text: And it wins for language practice. Pick a language and talk. The AI answers in that language: a patient conversation partner who never gets bored and corrects you gently.

beats.narration_text: But typing wins when you need to keep something. A plan, an address, a recipe. Voice vanishes, text stays. If you will need it later, type it, or ask for it in writing.

beats.narration_text: Typing wins when the instructions must be exact. A password, a number, a name spelled right. Speech recognition still mishears things. Ears make mistakes that eyes do not.

beats.narration_text: And typing wins in public. On a train, in a waiting room, at your desk among coworkers. Nobody wants to hear your side of the conversation, so type quietly.

beats.narration_text: Three tips for talking well. One: speak in full thoughts, not fragments. Finish the idea before you pause. A complete sentence gives the AI something real to work with.

shot.visual_intent: Broken dim wave fragments on the left; one complete ink wave on the right, running into a page.

beats.narration_text: Two: interrupt freely. If it starts rambling, just talk over it. Say shorter, or skip to the point. A voice conversation is allowed to be rude in a way typing never is.

shot.visual_intent: A long wave runs across the stage; an ink arrow slashes through it and the far half fades out; the label 'interrupt' sits above.

beats.narration_text: Three: when you are done, ask for a summary. Say, summarize what we decided, in text. The spoken part did the thinking. The written part does the remembering.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Open voice mode in the AI app you use, and brainstorm out loud with me for two minutes: a weekend trip, a project, or a gift idea. Then say: summarize our plan in text. Then check two things yourself. Did speaking beat typing for getting ideas out? And is the summary something you would actually keep?
